label: Thermal Dimorphism
rows: Natural habitat; saprobic (free-living), mycelial phase; reproduces by sporulation
Animal habitat; parasitic, yeast phase; reproduces by budding or endospores

mnemonic.hook: Mold in the cold, yeast in the heat.
mnemonic.breaks: The slides name thermal dimorphism as the true pathogens' trait (slides 5, 24); slide 27 grows the Histoplasma mold below 35 °C.

label: Levels of Fungal Infection, Shallow to Deep
rows: Contamination of the skin or hair surface
Tinea versicolor, white and black piedra
Stratum corneum, occasionally the upper dermis (keratin only)
Contamination of the skin or hair surface
Subcutaneous tissue, after a puncture wound
Inoculated into skin or nails: trauma
From the lungs into the circulation: brain, kidneys, other organs
Respiratory: spores inhaled from the air

mnemonic.hook: Touched, touched, stabbed, breathed: the deeper it goes, the harder it got in.
key: superficial: contamination of hair or the skin surface
mnemonic.breaks: Slide 14 gives cutaneous and superficial one shared portal; true-pathogen spores can also be inoculated into broken skin (slide 24).

label: World Health Organization Fungal Priority Pathogens List (2022)
rows: Cryptococcus neoformans (number one, slide 56) · Aspergillus fumigatus (number three, slide 60) · Candida albicans · Candida auris
Other Candida species · Eumycetoma causative agents · Fusarium species · Histoplasma species · Mucorales (mucormycosis opportunists)
Coccidioides · Cryptococcus gattii · Pneumocystis jirovecii · Paracoccidioides species

mnemonic.hook: Critical: CACC (Crypto, Aspergillus, and two Candidas). High: Can Every Fungus Hide Mold? Medium: two Cs and two Ps.
mnemonic.breaks: Two Cryptococcus species sit in different tiers: neoformans critical, gattii medium.

label: The Four True (Dimorphic) Fungal Pathogens
rows: Eastern and central United States; Latin America, Africa
Moist, nitrogen-rich soil with bird and bat guano
Most common true pathogen; NOT person to person; yeast multiplies inside phagocytes
Southwestern United States, Mexico, Central and South America
Alkaline, salty soil of semiarid, hot climates; dust
Arthroconidia in soil, spherules with endospores in the lungs; most need no treatment
Midwestern and southeastern United States, southern Canada; also reported in South and Central America, Africa, the Middle East
Forest soil, decaying wood, animal manure
May be mistaken for lung cancer on chest X-ray; skin nodules, later bone and nervous system
Central and South America (Brazil, Colombia, Venezuela, Argentina, Paraguay)
Cool, humid soil; inhaled (lung) or inoculated (skin)
The rarest primary mycosis; rural farm workers, poor nutrition; usually mild, self-limiting

key: Histoplasma: bird (and bat) droppings, the Ohio Valley
Coccidioides: the semiarid, hot Southwest, dust
Blastomyces: forest soil and rotting wood of the Midwest and Southeast
mnemonic.breaks: Histoplasma also lives in Latin America and Africa; Coccidioides reaches South America too (slide 30); Blastomyces has been reported beyond North America (slide 33).

label: Tinea by Body Site: the Latin Names
tag: ★ Classification · Lecture 15 · slides 43–45 (“Focus on the Latin names”)
rows: Scalp and hair-bearing head; hair may be lost; common in children
Chin and beard of adult males; mainly from animals
Inflamed, red ring lesions on smooth skin; contact, clothing, bedding
'Jock itch': groin and scrotum; athletes, crowded living
Public surfaces; between the digits and on the soles; rare where people go barefoot
Paired with tinea pedis: public surfaces, between the digits
Persistent colonization that distorts the nail bed; nail extensions a portal of entry

mnemonic.hook: Each Latin name hides an English word you already know.
mnemonic.breaks: Cruris is a sound-alike, not the real root. Tinea versicolor is not on this list: it is a superficial yeast infection (Malassezia), not a dermatophyte.

label: Superficial Mycoses
rows: Mild, chronic scaling and mottling of the skin; also folliculitis, psoriasis, seborrheic dermatitis
Whitish or colored masses on pubic or axillary hair (also body, beard, mustache, eyebrows)
Dark-brown to black gritty nodules, mainly on scalp hairs

rows.note: Both piedras (piedra = stone) are non-contagious, linked to poor hygiene (oily hair products, tight hats or veils), and uncommon in the United States.

mnemonic.hook: Versicolor changes color; the stones are white below and black on top.
key: white piedra on pubic and axillary hair (Trichosporon)
mnemonic.breaks: White piedra also occurs on the beard, mustache and eyebrows (slide 49), so "below" is only its main site.

label: Opportunists and What Predisposes to Them (Table 22.3)
rows: Antibiotic therapy, catheters, diabetes, corticosteroids, immunosuppression
Leukemia, corticosteroids, tuberculosis, immunosuppression, intravenous drug abuse
Diabetes, cancer, corticosteroids, intravenous therapy, third-degree burns

rows.note: Footnotes: anti-inflammatory drugs are given for chronic lung disease and to transplant patients; immunosuppression includes acquired immunodeficiency syndrome and genetic conditions.

mnemonic.hook: Steroids open the door for all four; then each has its own key.
key: Cleared bacteria and Catheters: antibiotic therapy, catheters
Leukemia and needles: leukemia, intravenous drug abuse
Zapped skin: third-degree burns, intravenous therapy
mnemonic.breaks: Diabetes is on three rows (not Aspergillus); tuberculosis on two (Aspergillus, Cryptococcus); immunosuppression on three (not Zygomycota).

label: Treatments Named on the Slides
rows: Amphotericin B, but most cases need no treatment
Heat packs, super-saturated potassium iodide; systemic: amphotericin B and/or itraconazole
Topical azoles for several weeks, oral antifungals if needed; debridement; ultraviolet light
Topical antifungals (superficial); amphotericin B and azoles (systemic)
Amphotericin B and fluconazole or another azole
Pentamidine (anti-protozoan) and co-trimoxazole (antibacterial): NOT traditional antifungals
Removal of affected tissue and amphotericin B
Long-term antifungal drug therapy and amputation may be required

rows.note: Aspergillosis: slide 60 lists amphotericin B and nystatin; current practice does not use nystatin for invasive disease (guide 15.23). No doses are taught.

mnemonic.hook: When in doubt, ampho B. The exceptions are the skin, the lung of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome, and the knife.
key: histoplasmosis, coccidioidomycosis, blastomycosis, paracoccidioidomycosis, systemic sporotrichosis, candidiasis, cryptococcosis, mucormycosis
topical azoles for tinea; topical antifungals for superficial candidiasis; potassium iodide and heat for sporotrichosis
The lung of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome
mnemonic.breaks: Coccidioidomycosis usually needs nothing at all; Paracoccidioides adds ketoconazole and sulfa drugs.

label: Fungal Toxins (Mycotoxicoses)
rows: Hepatotoxic and carcinogenic; lethal to poultry and livestock (turkeys, ducklings, pigs, calves); may be a co-factor in human liver cancer
Rye and other grains contaminated by Claviceps
Sick building syndrome ('black mold', not mucormycosis); can cause severe hematologic and neurological damage

rows.note: Mycotoxicoses come from INGESTING or INHALING fungal toxins. Not all building molds are toxic, and not all building illness is fungal.

mnemonic.hook: A-E-S: Aflatoxin Attacks the liver, Ergot Enters the mind, Stachybotrys makes the building Sick.
